rounds.text: Soni Medicare is currently undergoing a significant operational turnaround, evidenced by a dramatic shift in profitability where quarterly operating margins surged to 18% in September 2026 from a negative 8% in the year-ago quarter [E27]. This momentum is further validated by a 185% year-over-year increase in net profit, which has contributed to a high recent return on equity [E8, E46]. The company is operating within a sector experiencing a strong macro tailwind, which provides a supportive environment for this improving performance [E50, E52]. Management has also demonstrated fiscal discipline by reducing total borrowings to Rs 12.32 Cr from Rs 12.95 Cr in the prior year [E33]. While the stock has seen a 38% compounded growth over the last three years, the current market sentiment remains cautious despite these accelerating results [E20, E51]. Conceded: the company faces challenges with negative operating cash flow, high debtor days, and inconsistent long-term return on equity [E31, E42, E43].

Soni Medicare Ltd is displaying the early, highly powerful hallmarks of an operational turnaround that the market has not yet fully priced in [E51]. Most notably, quarterly operating margins have surged to 18% in September 2026 compared to a negative 8% in the year-ago quarter, marking a dramatic 26 percentage point expansion [E27]. This sudden profitability acceleration is underscored by stellar recent performance metrics, featuring a 185% year-on-year surge in net profit and a 12% year-on-year increase in sales [E45, E46, E51]. Furthermore, management is actively deleveraging the balance sheet, with borrowings reduced to Rs 12.32 Cr in September 2026 down from Rs 12.95 Cr a year prior [E33]. These green shoots are developing against a robust sectoral backdrop, as the healthcare sector enjoys a strong tailwind score of nearly +1 with median sector profit growth sitting at 19% [E50, E53]. Conceded: trailing twelve months sales growth has contracted by 17% and free cash flow remains negative at Rs -0.55 Cr [E16, E32].

Conceded: quarterly operating margins reached 18% in September 2026 [E27] and net profit showed a 185% year-on-year surge [E46]. However, this single-quarter pop masks an inconsistent yearly and quarterly operating-margin trend [E28, E29], rendering the supposed turnaround unstable. Furthermore, the claim of operational healing is entirely undermined by a devastating trailing twelve-month sales contraction of 17% [E16] and a multi-year sales slump that includes a 3-year compounded decline of 4% [E15]. The bull's invocation of balance sheet deleveraging ignores the reality of persistent negative cash generation, evidenced by free cash flow sitting deeply in the red at Rs -0.55 Cr [E32] and operating cash flow at Rs -0.26 Cr [E31]. Finally, pointing to sector tailwinds [E50] cannot excuse company-specific destruction of capital, highlighted by a staggering 3-year median return on equity of -117% [E24] and an abysmal TTM ROE reading of -10880% [E12].
